working_title: One Text, Two Tokenizers: GPT-2 and GPT-4
story_question: How do the GPT-2 and GPT-4 tokenizers segment the same fixed multilingual sample, and which encoding choices explain any count differences?
case: Compare the gpt2 and cl100k_base encodings assigned to GPT-2 and GPT-4 in a pinned tiktoken source revision, using the same declared English, Hindi and Japanese strings for both.
place_period_version: OpenAI tiktoken repository commit 4e71bbe0c078468e00fefbf94b39849389f346e5, inspected 2026-10-24; historical code mapping, not a claim about current hosted model availability or billing.
intended_audience: General adult viewers who want to understand why words and tokens are different units.
purpose: Show a reproducible difference in segmentation, then explain the vocabulary, pre-tokenization and byte-level boundaries without claiming access to a proprietary model's internal behavior.
evidence_gaps: Run both pinned encodings on the exact Unicode test strings and save token IDs, byte spans, counts, code version and execution environment.
Check normalization and visually similar Unicode forms separately; do not infer language quality or model capability from token count alone.
If the script discusses pricing or current product models, obtain separate dated primary documentation before making those claims.
blocking_gaps: No reproducible token-count measurements or claim ledger have been completed for the selected sample.
readiness_note: Official source-code access and the historical model-to-encoding mapping were checked. The comparison is selected, but its measurements and scripted claims are not verified; keep this idea in researching status.
